payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism. An independent audit retracted the initial cycle-life claim and established 8,400 as the corrected governing figure. The chemistry delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating limitation is a 4 °C floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
